description: Would love for participants whom are passionate about coding (Nextjs & React preferably) and space exploration to join my team!
summary: Lunar Explorer makes the Moon’s south pole explorable through a realistic simulation of terrain, sunlight, shadows, and Earth visibility. Built on NASA data and astronomical calculations, it shows how the Sun’s elevation and direction, surrounding ridges, lunar curvature, and changing time shape local conditions. Users move from orbital views to rover height, watch conditions evolve, and compare candidate landing locations and dates. They can investigate visibility windows, explore solar-power potential under stated equipment assumptions, and evaluate rover journeys. A map-connected AI assistant operates the workspace and explains results using scientific tools and cited evidence. By bringing physical simulation, visual explanation, and scenario comparison together, Lunar Explorer helps mission-concept teams, educators, and the public understand where and when lunar exploration may be possible.
details:
Lunar Explorer helps people experience the conditions behind a lunar landing decision. Move from an orbital overview to a rover’s perspective, advance the mission clock, and watch the Sun skim the skyline, shadows shift across the terrain, and Earth move into or out of view.

Realistic conditions with a scientific foundation. NASA terrain is represented at true scale, while astronomical calculations determine the Sun’s and Earth’s positions for the selected location and time. The simulation accounts for Sun elevation and direction, lunar curvature, nearby and distant ridges, instrument height, and the apparent size of both bodies. Visibility calculations include partial obstruction and Earth eclipsing the Sun. In Sunlight mode, the visible Sun, illumination, and local shadows follow the same calculated geometry and mission clock.

Understand the consequences of a choice. Users can compare locations and dates, examine sunlight and Earth-view windows, identify interruptions, and inspect the terrain responsible. Equipment scenarios reveal how panel and antenna height affect visibility. Solar-output estimates consider Sun distance, panel orientation, area, efficiency, and losses, thus connecting environmental conditions to power-generation potential.

Explore alternatives with an AI assistant. Natural-language requests can navigate the map, retrieve measurements, compare scenarios, and propose routes for numerical evaluation. Results remain connected to inspectable calculations, sources, and assumptions. Users can choose to manually control the map or delegate tasks to the assistant.

Extend landing analysis into surface exploration. Route tools check slope, roughness, sunlight, and Earth visibility at the rover’s expected arrival times, including travel and waits. Independent replay with finer sampling checks proposed journeys; the included Faustini-rim demonstration makes this workflow inspectable.

Built with TypeScript, Next.js, React, Three.js, and a Python/SPICE scientific pipeline, Lunar Explorer brings simulation, explanation, and comparison into one browser workspace. It supports education and early mission studies.
